messages.author: 484c91357ac83f6b
messages.subject: fixture valid.values
parts:
According to some tests I've done, Stan's fixture_distr ValidValues test
gets the values from different indexes (of the vector param) all mixed
up but doesn't say so.

Is this intended behaviour?

messages.author: 484c91357ac83f6b
messages.subject: Re: fixture valid.values
parts:
Example:



void valid_values(vector<vector<double> >& parameters,
vector<double>& log_prob) {
vector<double> param(5);

// using R: RWiener::dwiener(1.1, 2.1, .3, .55, .4, give_log=TRUE)
param[0] = 1.1; // y
param[1] = 2.1; // alpha
param[2] = .3; // tau
param[3] = .55; // beta
param[4] = .4; // delta
parameters.push_back(param);
log_prob.push_back(-0.892976431870503); // expected log_prob

param[0] = 2.1; // y
param[1] = 4.1; // alpha
param[2] = 1.9; // tau
param[3] = .05; // beta
param[4] = .1; // delta
parameters.push_back(param);
log_prob.push_back(-34.6843978137965); // expected log_prob

---------------------------------------

Then, we run the tests and get

[ RUN ]
AgradDistributionWiener_v_95/AgradDistributionTestFixture/0.ValidValues


y_vec1.1
tau_vec1.9 [[[SHOULD HAVE BEEN .3!!!!]]]


./test/prob/test_fixture_distr.hpp:110: Failure
Expected: ({ lp = TestClass.template log_prob <true,T0,T1,T2,T3,T4,T5>
(p0,p1,p2,p3,p4,p5); }) doesn't throw an exception.
Actual: it throws.
Valid parameters failed at index: 0 -- (1.1000000000000001,
2.1000000000000001, 0.29999999999999999, 0.55000000000000004,
0.40000000000000002)

On 2015-10-12 08:34 PM, Marco Inacio wrote:
> According to some tests I've done, Stan's fixture_distr ValidValues
> test gets the values from different indexes (of the vector param) all
> mixed up but doesn't say so.
>
> Is this intended behaviour?

messages.author: 484c91357ac83f6b
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: fixture valid.values
parts:
> Hi Marco,
>
> Sorry for the delay. Yes, that was how I implemented it. I didn't know how to generally generate sets of valid inputs, but maybe that's what I should have done.
>
> That test code is really hairy and could use a rewrite at some point.

OK, I was just afraid that this was a mistake rather than by design. The
only problem than is that the error message does not tell us that the
parameters from different indexes (of the vector param) were mixed.
> Were you able to figure out the problem you were having?

Yes, the problem was that since the function was mixing parameter from
different indexes, sometimes tau was greater than y (which throws), I'll
fix this by making every y greater than every tau for all indexes.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: fixture valid.values
parts:
I think the way to do this in general is to randomly generate
valid inputs based on constraints. I don't know that we have any
functions with dependent constraints other than Pareto (which has
a lower-bound parameter).

Just broadcasting a single test case would be nice to maintain
constraints, but I don't think it's a sufficient test.

- Bob
